name: Hyrox-style fitness racing
aliases: Hyrox / indoor fitness racing (8 x 1 km runs + 8 stations)
topicKeys: phrase:hyrox indoor fitness racing 8 x 1 km runs 8 stations
summary: A standardized indoor race (eight 1 km runs alternating with eight functional workout stations) that has turned gym-goers into first-time 'fitness racers' who train for months toward an event.
what: Hyrox races use the same format everywhere: 1 km run, then a station (ski erg, sled push, sled pull, burpee broad jumps, row, farmers carry, sandbag lunges, wall balls), repeated eight times. That makes times comparable and gives newcomers a concrete training target. Participants track run splits and station times and follow 8-16 week plans.

origin.text: A branded race series whose 2025/26 season is reported at more than 1.5 million athletes, with the 2026/27 calendar expanding to 107 race weekends including new US host cities.

adopters.text: Gym members, runners and CrossFit-adjacent athletes looking for a goal race; gyms affiliating to offer training (UK affiliates 18 to 120 in a year).

spread.text: Global press (Malaysia, Thailand, Australia, UK trade press, US functional-fitness media) with record single-event turnouts in Asia. US-specific participation figures were not found; US growth is shown only by new host cities.

trajectory.text: Globally surging: reported participation of 1.5M in 2025/26 with more than 2M expected in 2026/27, plus multi-week residencies for demand. The US is a smaller, growing slice (new San Diego and Portland events), so the US trajectory is less certain.

productDemand.text: People pay for preparation: several independent training books, an official-partner ebook, Notion trackers and apps exist, and sellers bundle printable checklists and calendars. That is supply-side evidence; direct sales figures were not observed.

competition.text: Moderate to high for training plans (books, Rogue ebook, apps). Narrower for physical logbooks and printable split trackers, though a logbook seller already targets the race-day log. The trademark limits keyword use for unofficial products.

gap.text: A paper or printable split-and-station logbook for first-time racers (16-week block, per-station PB tracker, compromised-run log, race-day checklist), sold as a January training gift, appears thinner than plans and apps. Training plans carry expertise and injury-liability expectations a solo creator should avoid.

window.estimate: Mid-Nov 2026 to Mar 2027 (holiday gifts, then New-Year race sign-ups); the format looks durable for multiple seasons.
window.reasoning: The 2026/27 season is underway and expanding; New-Year fitness goals line up with spring races. KDP paperbacks take days to go live and ship quickly, which fits a December listing.
invalidators: Brand enforcement against unofficial products using the name
US participation stays small relative to Europe/Asia
Apps (including official ones) make paper logs irrelevant to this tech-forward audience
window.seasonality: January resolution peak; race-specific spikes near US event dates (not verified).

rights.note: HYROX is a brand with official partners (PUMA, Rogue). Do not use the name or logo in product titles or designs. Describe the product generically ('for 8-station fitness races') and rely on descriptive keywords; any use of the name, even in tags, carries takedown risk. Avoid prescriptive training or medical claims.

timing.rationale: Season expanding and the New-Year window is close, but US-specific growth evidence is thin.

buyerIntent.rationale: Paid race participation at reported scale (1.5M athletes worldwide, 2025/26) shows people spend on the activity. There is no evidence of demand for paper logbooks specifically, and US-only figures were not found.

supplyGap.rationale: Plans, apps and Notion trackers are present; a paper-log niche may be open but is unverified.

productFit.rationale: Logbooks are easy to make; the trademark limits discovery, and plans need expertise.

durability.rationale: Participation reported growing season over season, with Olympic ambitions and gym affiliate growth.

economics.rationale: KDP and printable margins are fine at $7-12; heavy competition from free apps caps pricing.

actionRationale: Real, durable participation growth, but US share, product-specific demand and how much the trademark limits keywords are unresolved. Build a generic fitness-race logbook in November for a mid-December KDP/Etsy launch aimed at New-Year racers rather than testing now.

products.buyer: First-time fitness racers training for a spring 2027 event, and gym partners buying them a gift
products.theme: 16-week fitness-race training log (KDP 6x9 paperback plus printable PDF): weekly plan grid, 8 run-split + 8 station time tracker per session, station PB pages, compromised-running log, race-day checklist and post-race reflection
products.whyBuy: A standardized format makes split tracking central to training, and January brings new sign-ups.
products.differentiation: Paper alternative to apps, focused on split and station tracking rather than prescribing workouts; no brand name used.
products.validationTest: Publish the printable on Etsy first ($7) with generic keywords; post 3 short videos showing a filled-in split page; check views and sales over 14 days before ordering a KDP proof.
products.continueIf: At least 3 printable sales or at least 300 views with 20+ favorites in 14 days.
products.pivotIf: Interest only in race-day pages: sell a $4 race-day checklist and pacing card pack.
products.stopIf: Under 100 views in 3 weeks, or any trademark complaint.
products.rightsNote: Never use 'HYROX' or its logo in titles, tags or designs; use generic station names.

products.theme: Race-day pacing kit: Google Sheets split calculator (target finish time to per-run and per-station targets), printable wrist/pace cards and a gear and fueling checklist
products.whyBuy: Newcomers want a concrete pacing plan for a standardized course; sellers already bundle checklists and cue cards as book bonuses.
products.differentiation: Cheap, single-purpose and race-week focused; complements apps rather than replacing them.
products.validationTest: List at $5 alongside the log; measure views and sales over 21 days.
products.pivotIf: Offer it as a free lead magnet for the logbook.
products.rightsNote: Generic language only; no brand marks; no medical or nutrition claims.

unresolved: US share of the 1.5M participants and US race dates for Jan-Apr 2027.
How strictly the brand enforces its trademark against unofficial logbooks on Etsy and Amazon.
Search demand for generic terms ('fitness race training log') versus the brand term.
Whether an app-first audience buys paper logs.
What the PUMA collection controversy was about.
